summary: Transport-neutral API DTO contract crates for HR, payroll, and accounting foundation flows.

findings: The API crates expose plain DTOs, enum mappings, and conversion methods into existing domain/app inputs instead of introducing a router or framework prematurely.
Contract tests assert observable JSON field names and enum labels so accidental public-shape drift is caught early.
Flat package names oya-hr-employment-api, oya-payroll-run-api, and oya-accounting-journal-api preserve per-service API ownership.
The slice creates provider-neutral boundary contracts before cloud/runtime adapters, matching API-first integration sequencing without deployment claims.

F3_adversarial.failing_fixture_id: serde contract assertions for renamed fields and enum labels
F3_adversarial.diagnostic_asserted: Tests fail if camelCase field names, SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE enum labels, validation error envelope shape, or domain/app conversion behavior drifts.
findings: cargo test --locked -p oya-hr-employment-api -p oya-payroll-run-api -p oya-accounting-journal-api passes 10 integration tests.

Request types are named after business actions: OnboardEmployeeRequest, LaborCompliancePlanRequest, PayrollTrialCloseRequest, PayrollJournalDraftRequest, JournalPostRequest, PayrollPostingRequest, and VatDeadlineRequest.
Each request owns an into_domain or into_command conversion, keeping handler code later thin and predictable.

Verification passed: cargo fmt, locked cargo test for all three API crates, clippy for each API crate with --all-targets and -D warnings, cargo tree, governance gates, cargo deny, JSON parse, and quality-marker scan.
Cargo.lock was refreshed by cargo for the new workspace package entries and already-present serde dependencies.

alternatives_named: publish OpenAPI files without typed Rust DTOs
F6_alternatives.selected_rationale: Rust DTO contracts give compile-time conversion checks and serde shape tests without coupling to transport or deployment choices.
rejected_reasons: An HTTP framework would add runtime/auth/deployment concerns that need separate evidence.
OpenAPI-only files would not prove conversion into existing domain/app inputs.

findings: DTOs carry tenant, legal-entity, evidence, source digest, and financial fields explicitly; runtime auth and rate limiting are not claimed by this transport-neutral slice.
No credentials, HTTP listener, external client, database, payment rail, or filing connector was introduced.

F8_performance.regression_baseline: No prior HR/payroll/accounting API DTO crates existed; no served latency or throughput claim is made.

findings.summary: DTO conversion is synchronous value movement over bounded request vectors; no network, async runtime, persistence, or polling loop introduced.

findings: All new public DTO fields carry data_class comments and catalogs classify HR as PII, payroll as PII plus FINANCIAL, and accounting as FINANCIAL.
The API layer does not claim legal compliance, tax-rate correctness, statutory filing, financial statement export, or live access-control enforcement.

Additive workspace members and catalog rows can be reverted by removing the three API crate directories, registry/per-service catalog rows, spec AC-07/decision-log additions, and Cargo.toml members. No migration or persisted data exists.
DTO contracts include validation error envelope shapes but do not emit logs, metrics, traces, or audit-chain records at runtime. Runtime observability remains a later adapter slice.
No external endpoint is deployed yet, so compatibility risk is limited to workspace consumers. The tests pin initial public JSON shapes before any runtime adapter ships.

M1_challenge_assumption.premise_stated: API DTO crates are useful before cloud integration only if they remain transport-neutral and prove conversion into current app/domain inputs.
M1_challenge_assumption.premise_evidence_ref: tasks/enterprise-microservices-plan.md#CS-ENT-API-001 + cargo tree output for each API crate
M1_challenge_assumption.do_nothing_consequence: Later HTTP/cloud adapters would either duplicate request contracts or bypass typed conversion into domain/app layers.
M1_challenge_assumption.upstream_fix_rejection_reason: Waiting for deployed HTTP adapters would couple contract work to auth, routing, SLO, and infrastructure evidence.

findings: Fits compositional ERP sequencing by placing a serializable admission boundary above domain and app foundations while preserving service separation.
Package names follow oya-<microservice>-<bounded-context>-api.
tasks/enterprise-microservices-plan.md and tasks/enterprise-microservices-todo.md document the API DTO slice and non-claims.
Implementation resides under microservices/hr|payroll|accounting/crates/*-api with matching per-service and central catalog rows.
No HTTP framework, router, auth middleware, persistence, Workflow client, audit emitter, filing connector, payment rail, or cloud runtime introduced.
API crates use workspace serde for serialization, serde_json only in tests, and inward dependencies on same-service app/domain crates where conversion tests require them.
registry/dependency-rationales.json explicitly allows serde and serde_json for the three transport-neutral API DTO crates; dependency-seam passes after that policy row update.
HR, Payroll, and Accounting specs gained AC-07 API DTO acceptance refs pointing to existing contract tests.
Conversion methods are deterministic field mappings with enum matches and no hidden global state.
